title: Pelagos Port Disbursement Intelligence Source Inventory & Governance Catalog
author: Pelagos Core Intelligence & Optimization Team
governance_policy: Non-synthetic port disbursement modeling; fail-closed missing data policy; strict separation between statutory disclosure and operational commercial permission

pilot_ports.lead_authority: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA)
Havenbedrijf Rotterdam N.V. (Port of Rotterdam Authority)
Port of Houston Authority (PHA) & Houston Pilots

taxonomic_categories.description: Statutory municipal or national dues assessed on vessel presence in port waters, typically based on Gross Tonnage (GT) and length of stay.
Compulsory navigation assistance fees for inbound, outbound, or shifting movements, billed by LOA, draft, GT, or fixed pilot unit.
Assistance tug services for berthing, unberthing, and escorting. Billed per tug per hour or per maneuver based on bollard pull.
Quay and terminal infrastructure charges assessed per foot or meter of LOA per 24-hour period, or per GT.
Fee assessed on cargo passing over the wharf or transferred between vessels, billed per metric or short ton.
Boatmen and shore line-handling services for securing and releasing vessel mooring lines at berth or buoys.
Dues for remaining at designated anchorage grounds, often subject to a free grace period (e.g. 24 or 48 hours).
Statutory fee for mandatory collection and treatment of ship-generated oily waste (Annex I), sewage (Annex IV), and garbage (Annex V).
Supply of potable fresh water via shore hydrant or water barge, billed per cubic meter plus delivery charge.
Statutory surcharge for International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) compliance, billed as flat fee or dockage percentage.

Commercial agent remuneration for vessel inward/outward clearance, supervisory attendance, and disbursement account processing under FONASBA / BIMCO standard agency agreements. Not a statutory port authority due; never generated as a universal fixed statutory fee.
National navigational infrastructure levies (e.g. UK Trinity House light dues, Indian light dues) assessed per call or period.
